dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Good afternoon. My name is Erin Lynch. I would like to inquire about a drainage problem near my home. I am at 320 Annandale Road, in the North End.
Okay, Ms. Lynch, 320 Annandale Road. What's going on there?

Since the storm on Sunday into Monday, the snow that turned to rain, water has been coming down the hill from the next street over. It runs straight down and into my yard. I am quite concerned about it.
So the water's coming off the hill from the neighboring street and into your yard. Is that still happening today, or was it mostly during the rain?

It was heaviest during the rain on Monday, but it has not fully stopped. There is still a steady trickle this afternoon. And the sidewalk in front of the house is a sheet of mud and grit. I cannot imagine anyone walking on it safely, especially if it freezes tonight.
Yeah, that'll get slick fast. A sheet of mud and grit on the sidewalk out front. Is there a storm drain close by, do you know? Maybe one that looks clogged?

There is a grate at the corner, [pause] I believe it is partly covered with leaves and gravel. Which brings me to my question. Is that a city drain or a state one? I would like to be certain I am calling the correct office.

Good question. Annandale Road is a city street as far as I know, so a drain on it would be ours. If the one on the next street is a state road, that could be different. Do you know the name of the street the water's coming from?
I am afraid I do not know it by name. It is the street that runs along the top of the hill, behind my property. I can look at the sign if you would like me to.

No need to go out in it. I'll note the location as the hill behind you and have somebody look at the drain at the corner and see where the runoff is originating. If it turns out to be a state drain, we'd pass it along to them ourselves.

That is very kind. I would appreciate that. I have been keeping track of every expense related to this in a spiral notebook, the sand, the gravel I bought, the time I have spent. I would like to know whether any of it is the city's responsibility.

Keep that notebook going, it's a good idea to write down dates and what you spent. I can't tell you about reimbursement, that's not something I handle, but I'll put in the work order and you'll have the record of your call.
Thank you. Would a work order be assigned a number that I can reference?

It will. Let me get it started. So, 320 Annandale Road, North End, runoff from the hill behind into the yard, mud and debris on the sidewalk, and a possibly clogged drain at the corner. Did I get that right?
Yes, that is entirely correct.
And is the best callback number the one you're calling from?
I am on my cell phone. The number is 401-555-0183.

401-555-0183. Got it. I'll have a crew take a look, probably within the next day or two, given the cleanup after the storm. If it freezes tonight and the sidewalk is really bad, call us back and we'll flag it.
I will do that. Thank you very much for your help, Ms. Medeiros.
You're welcome, Ms. Lynch. You take care, and stay off that sidewalk.
I shall. Good afternoon.
